problem: Collaborative human-robot exploration dialogue is usually done via teleoperation or Wizard-of-Oz setups; there is no automated, data-driven spoken dialogue interface that turns natural language into robot navigation actions and asks for clarification, testable safely in simulation.
motivation: Full teleoperation needs many human resources and high-bandwidth, reliable links, which are unavailable in disaster relief and search-and-rescue. High-level natural language tasking with low-bandwidth multimodal feedback reduces human load and communication requirements.
key_idea: Replace the human dialogue-manager and robot-navigator wizards with an NPCEditor statistical text classifier trained on Wizard-of-Oz dialogues, bridged via ros2vhmsg to a ROS/Gazebo simulated Jackal robot that executes mapped motion commands.
insight: A simple retrieval-style classifier trained on about 1,500 Wizard-of-Oz utterance pairs suffices for a constrained domain (86% held-out accuracy), handling disfluencies and metric commands. It is limited to responses seen in training and cannot handle landmark-based instructions. No ablations are reported.
method: ASR: Google ASR API adaptation (from the Virtual Human toolkit) converts unconstrained spoken Commander input to text.

NPCEditor NLU/DM: statistical text classifier using cross-language retrieval models, trained on 1,500 Commander/DM-Wizard pairs from phases 1-2; a hybrid classifier outputs a translation to the RN plus feedback to the Commander, extended for multi-floor dialogue.
Dialogue policy: simple rules pairing RN commands with positive feedback ('Moving...', 'Turning...') and issuing clarification requests for underspecified commands.
ros2vhmsg: macOS bridge that subscribes/publishes on both the VHMSG (ActiveMQ) and ROS brokers, translating text and navigation messages, with metadata tags to avoid loops.

Automated Robot Navigator: rospy script mapping predefined instruction strings to ROS Twist messages (forward/back 1-10 ft, turns 45/90/180/360 degrees) and image requests; no collision avoidance or landmark support.
Simulation: Gazebo environment modeled on the real space, a simulated Clearpath Jackal with IMU, camera and Hokuyo LIDAR, and rviz visualization for the Commander display.

setting.backbone: NPCEditor statistical text classifier (cross-language retrieval model, trained) + Google ASR API
setting.training_data: 1,500 Commander utterance / DM-Wizard response pairs from Wizard-of-Oz phases 1 and 2
setting.observation: Spoken language commands; LIDAR map and on-request static camera photos shown to the Commander
setting.action_space: Predefined ROS Twist commands (move 1-10 ft, turn 45/90/180/360 deg) and image capture

numbers_note: Demo paper with no benchmark results; only a held-out NLU classification accuracy of 86% is reported, which is not a navigation benchmark.
results: The system is a working demo where spoken commands drive a simulated Jackal with clarification dialogues. The NLU classifier reaches 86% accuracy on a held-out test set. No navigation benchmark comparison is given.
limitations: Responses are limited to those seen in the training data, and landmark-based instructions are not supported by the automated navigator.
No collision avoidance, and the mapping covers only predefined metric commands.
No quantitative navigation evaluation, and the system is tested only in simulation so far.
builds_on: Wizard-of-Oz two-wizard studies (Marge et al. 2016; Bonial et al. 2017)
